title: Pick the camera description
scenario: A portrait is meant to feel calm and professional for a speaker page. Both prompts below describe the same person and setting; only the camera language differs.
task: Which prompt will guide the model better?
promptA: Portrait of a woman holding a coffee cup, really good camera, professional, stunning, high detail, some angle, nice background blur maybe.
promptB: Eye-level portrait of a woman holding a coffee cup, 85mm portrait feel with a softly blurred café behind her, soft window light from the left, shallow depth of field.

feedback.a: Praise stacked on vague camera hints — “some angle”, “maybe”, “stunning” — describes no decision the model can act on. The result is luck, and you cannot debug luck.
feedback.b: One angle (eye level), one lens idea (85mm feel), one light direction and one depth decision. Four coherent choices, each individually fixable if the result disappoints.

hints: Count the actual camera decisions in each prompt, not the adjectives.
explanation: Camera language works when it states decisions: where the viewer stands, what lens that suggests, what stays sharp. Praise and vague hedges move none of those dials. The better prompt is shorter and far more specific — and when the portrait comes back wrong, you can change exactly one thing instead of rewriting everything.
